# core/strsort.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/strsort.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Sorting pieces of a text in dictionary order (byte
order), for sorted word lists, directory listings and `sort | uniq`.

`spans_order` does not move the spans: it returns the indices `0..n` in
the order of the texts they name, so the same order can be applied to
several parallel vectors. It is insertion sort, quadratic in the worst
case and fast on short or nearly sorted lists; for a large list, compute
a number for each string and use `sort_by_key_u64`.

What is proved: the result is a permutation of `0..n` (`same_elems`
against the identity, so no index is lost or repeated), and neighbours in
the result are in order (`span_le`, which reads the bytes of both spans:
at the first byte where they differ the earlier one is smaller, and a
span that is a proper prefix of another comes first). `span_cmp` proves
the same relation for one pair. Not proved: that the order holds between
elements that are not neighbours (that needs `span_le` to be transitive,
which no proof here has shown).

`import "core/strsort.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/sort.bastio](core-sort.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/spancmp.bastio](core-spancmp.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`spans_order`](#spans_order) | The indices `0..n` of `spans`, so that each span's text is at or after the previous one's. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `spans_order`

```bastio
fn spans_order(b: &Bytes, spans: &Vec[Span]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(spans) ==> span_in(vget(spans, k), b)
  ensures vlen(result) == vlen(spans)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(result) ==> vget(result, k) < vlen(spans)
  ensures forall x: u64 :: x < vlen(spans) ==> vcount(result, x) == 1
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k + 1 < vlen(result) ==> span_le(b, vget(spans, vget(result, k)).start, vget(spans, vget(result, k)).end, vget(spans, vget(result, k + 1)).start, vget(spans, vget(result, k + 1)).end)
```

The indices `0..n` of `spans`, so that each span's text is at or after
the previous one's. Equal texts keep their order.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("pear apple fig apple");
let words = bytes_split(b, 32);   // at each space
let order = spans_order(b, words);
let mut ok = vec_len(order) == 4;
if ok {
  let w0 = vec_get(words, vec_get(order, 0));
  let w3 = vec_get(words, vec_get(order, 3));
  ok = bytes_span_eq_str(b, w0.start, w0.end, "apple")
    && bytes_span_eq_str(b, w3.start, w3.end, "pear");
}
vec_free(order);
vec_free(words);
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

## Specification functions

### `le_at`

```bastio
spec fn le_at(b: &Bytes, cs: &Vec[u64], ce: &Vec[u64], a: u64, c: u64) -> bool {
  span_le(b, vget(cs, a), vget(ce, a), vget(cs, c), vget(ce, c))
}
```

Elements `a` and `c` of the vectors `cs` and `ce` (the starts and ends of
a list of spans) are in order.

## Internals

### `spans_insert`

```bastio
fn spans_insert(b: &Bytes, ss: &Vec[u64], es: &Vec[u64], v: &mut Vec[u64], cs: &mut Vec[u64], ce: &mut Vec[u64], i: u64)
  requires i < vlen(v) && vlen(cs) == vlen(v) && vlen(ce) == vlen(v) && vlen(ss) == vlen(es)
  requires forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) < vlen(ss) && vget(cs, k) == vget(ss, vget(v, k)) && vget(ce, k) == vget(es, vget(v, k))
  requires forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(cs, k) <= vget(ce, k) && vget(ce, k) <= blen(b) && (k + 1 < i ==> le_at(b, cs, ce, k, k + 1))
  ensures vlen(v) == vlen(old(v)) && vlen(cs) == vlen(v) && vlen(ce) == vlen(v)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(v, k) < vlen(ss) && vget(cs, k) == vget(ss, vget(v, k)) && vget(ce, k) == vget(es, vget(v, k))
  ensures forall x: u64 :: vcount(v, x) == vcount(old(v), x)
  ensures forall x: u64 :: vcount(cs, x) == vcount(old(cs), x)
  ensures forall x: u64 :: vcount(ce, x) == vcount(old(ce), x)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(v) ==> vget(cs, k) <= vget(ce, k) && vget(ce, k) <= blen(b) && (k < i ==> le_at(b, cs, ce, k, k + 1))
```

Internal: moves element `i` of the three parallel vectors (an index, and
the start and end of the span it names) down past every neighbour whose
span is larger, so that the first `i + 1` are in order if the first `i`
were. The spans are carried along with their indices, so that every
quantifier here is about plain vectors of numbers: the solver does not
cope with the span of `v[k]` looked up through `v`.
